forces.title: Persistent patient recruitment pressure in clinical trials continues
forces.description: Clinical trials face persistent pressure in patient recruitment and site capacity, along with protocol amendments, leading to delays. This is attributed to intensifying competition for a narrower, more precisely defined patient population, a structural feature of modern trial design. This challenge impacts healthcare BPO and KPO providers involved in clinical trial support, requiring innovative approaches beyond just increased spending.
forces.source_title: Clinical Trials Face Persistent Challenges—and New Opportunities

forces.title: AI adoption increasing in clinical trials for operations and recruitment
forces.description: AI and machine learning adoption is picking up in clinical trials, with CROs and sponsors increasingly using these technologies. While still primarily in under 25% of studies, the focus is shifting towards roles that directly touch trial operations and patients, such as trial monitoring and patient recruitment. This trend presents a structural shift for healthcare BPO and KPO providers, demanding integration of AI capabilities to enhance efficiency and effectiveness in their clinical trial support services.
forces.source_title: Clinical Trials Face Persistent Challenges—and New Opportunities

forces.title: AI enables faster, better business decisions and operational improvements
forces.description: AI's true potential lies in enabling organizations to make better decisions faster, not merely reducing labor costs. This improves the use of existing assets, increases organizational flexibility, and allows companies to capture opportunities quicker than competitors. For BPO providers, this means AI can significantly enhance the value of outsourced processes, moving beyond task automation to provide strategic business outcomes and driving demand for AI-integrated BPO services across various operational domains like customer service and order-to-cash.
forces.source_title: The decision dividend: How AI creates economic value

forces.title: Outsourced domains are attractive starting points for AI redesign
forces.description: Domains already operated through outsourcing or offshoring often provide attractive starting points for deploying AI and redesigning operating models. These areas can typically be redesigned faster and with lower organizational disruption compared to insourced functions. This is a significant tailwind for BPO providers, as clients may increasingly look to their outsourced partners to lead AI-driven transformation within existing business processes, leveraging the BPO provider's scale and expertise to implement AI more efficiently.

forces.title: AI transformation mandate boosts enterprise shared services importance
forces.description: Scaling AI is an executive mandate, and enterprise shared services are uniquely positioned to capture this opportunity. AI requires strong process and data foundations, which centralized shared services provide by standardizing workflows and consolidating data. This transforms shared services from 'transaction factories' into 'AI deployment platforms' across functions, including specialized areas like regulatory documentation and clinical operations, making the adoption of mature shared services models a critical structural shift for BPO providers to enable AI for clients.
forces.source_title: Enterprise Shared Services in Medtech: The Only Wrong Move Is Standing Still

forces.title: M&A integration demands drive need for enterprise shared services
forces.description: For industries like medtech where inorganic growth is a strategic imperative, the ability to integrate acquisitions quickly and effectively is invaluable. Companies with mature enterprise shared services organizations are better positioned to integrate acquired businesses into common platforms, scale standardized processes, and capture synergies sooner. This creates a repeatable integration approach. This demand for efficient M&A integration acts as a tailwind for BPO providers who can offer standardized and scalable shared services to streamline post-acquisition operational consolidation for their clients.
forces.source_title: Enterprise Shared Services in Medtech: The Only Wrong Move Is Standing Still

forces.title: Healthcare RCM shifts to core strategic enabler amidst margin pressure
forces.description: Healthcare revenue cycle management (RCM) is undergoing a structural shift, evolving from a back-office function to a core strategic enabler. This is due to sustained margin pressure, new regulatory requirements, and dynamic reimbursement complexities. Financial resilience for care delivery organizations now demands building integrated revenue excellence across front-end, middle, and back-end processes. This significant shift increases the strategic importance of RCM BPO providers who can offer comprehensive and integrated solutions to manage these complexities and improve financial outcomes for healthcare clients.
forces.source_title: Healthcare revenue cycle management at a strategic turning point: Survey insights

forces.title: Outsourcing remains crucial for healthcare RCM capabilities
forces.description: Despite growing emphasis on automation in healthcare RCM, outsourcing remains crucial for acquiring necessary capabilities; only 6% of respondents plan to reduce outsourcing due to technology. Furthermore, 60% of RCM leaders expect to change their outsourcing approach over the next three years, with three-quarters of that group planning to expand their outsourcing efforts. This indicates a strong and growing demand for RCM BPO, particularly for scaled platforms that can integrate services and automation to address pain points like denials, A/R follow-up, coding, and eligibility/authorization.
forces.source_title: Healthcare revenue cycle management at a strategic turning point: Survey insights

forces.title: Challenges temper ROI expectations for AI in RCM
forces.description: Expectations for the magnitude and pace of ROI from AI and automation in healthcare RCM have tempered, facing barriers such as financial constraints, interoperability challenges, staff training, and change management. This moderation suggests that AI enablement is a phased transformation rather than an out-of-the-box solution. For BPO providers, this means a need for prudent, diligent investment in AI solutions with clear, demonstrable value and realistic timelines for ROI, focusing on credible near-term impact to maintain client support and avoid 'pilot purgatory'.
forces.source_title: Healthcare revenue cycle management at a strategic turning point: Survey insights

forces.title: AI adoption reshaping HR processes and functions
forces.description: AI tools are increasingly being deployed in HR functions, including resume screening, job description drafting, policy formulation, learning personalization, chatbots, and inclusion audits. While currently small-scale, the appetite for AI is growing due to its potential to go beyond previous technological breakthroughs, enabling reskilling at scale and handling routine employee queries to free HR professionals for strategic tasks. This represents a significant structural shift for HR BPO providers, requiring them to integrate AI to enhance service delivery and efficiency.

forces.title: Cultural resistance and scaling challenges impede AI in HR
forces.description: Despite momentum, the adoption of AI in HR faces obstacles, including cultural resistance (employees fearing replacement), leadership alignment issues, and difficulty in measuring ROI and scaling pilots beyond small experiments. Laying AI onto outdated workflows risks amplifying inefficiencies. For HR BPO providers, addressing these challenges requires human-first solutions, transparency, co-creation with employees, and a willingness to rethink work structures rather than just incremental AI adoption to achieve enterprise-wide transformation.

forces.title: UK's global leadership in financial/professional services eroding
forces.description: The UK's financial and related professional services industry faces a critical juncture, with its global competitive edge eroding due to factors like geopolitical volatility, protectionism, regulatory fragmentation, and intensifying competition from other financial centers. Despite its strengths, overall industry growth has stalled, and the UK risks losing its global leadership in emerging specialisms and digital infrastructure if it doesn't act with greater ambition and speed on regulatory reform and innovation. This broader decline impacts BPO components within financial and legal services.
forces.source_title: No time to lose: Reasserting UK leadership in financial and related professional services

forces.title: Technology fundamentally rewires market infrastructure and blurs sector boundaries
forces.description: Technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) and distributed ledger technology (DLT) are fundamentally rewiring market infrastructure, giving rise to new tokenised digital asset classes. Simultaneously, traditional boundaries between financial services, professional services, and technology providers are blurring as they converge around shared platforms, data, and capital pools. This structural change demands that BPO providers in these sectors rapidly adapt their offerings, integrate new technologies, and develop more holistic, platform-based solutions to stay competitive and relevant in an evolving market landscape.
forces.source_title: No time to lose: Reasserting UK leadership in financial and related professional services

forces.title: Private equity interest driving consolidation in Business and Professional Services
forces.description: Private equity (PE) interest in the Business and Professional Services (BPS) sector continues to build, particularly in accounting services. This consolidation activity among mid-sized firms is driven by the appeal of steady, recurring revenues from essential, repeatable services that provide reliable cash flows. PE investors also see further upside through the adoption of emerging technologies that can enhance efficiency and deliver better client solutions. This creates M&A opportunities and a demand for efficiency for BPO providers in the sector.

forces.title: Technology transforming BPS workplaces and task execution
forces.description: Emerging innovations, including generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI), agentic systems, and edge computing, are profoundly transforming workplaces and how tasks are performed across the Business and Professional Services (BPS) sector. This includes the development of law-firm specific AI tools and the anticipation of more specialized, sector-specific systems for accounting, consulting, and facilities management. This technological evolution represents a structural change that drives efficiency, competitiveness, and necessitates continuous adaptation and integration of new capabilities for BPO providers.

forces.title: Stablecoins enable efficient global payroll and B2B payments
forces.description: Digital currencies, specifically stablecoins, are moving into a new stage of adoption, delivering programmable money with practical uses in cross-border remittances, business-to-business (B2B) payments, global payroll, and corporate treasury. Adoption is accelerating fastest in cross-border flows, with stablecoin-based B2B payments seeing a 30-fold increase in two years. This represents a significant tailwind for BPO providers offering global payroll and F&A outsourcing services, as stablecoins offer potential for near-instant settlement, lower costs, and increased efficiency in international transactions.
forces.source_title: Global Payments Report 2025: The Future Is (Anything but) Stable

viewpoints.title: Enterprise shared services are crucial for medtech growth, AI, and simplification
viewpoints.description: Bain views enterprise shared services as critical for medtech companies to navigate margin pressure, acquisition debt, and new AI opportunities. By centralizing and standardizing support services (finance, HR, IT, and knowledge-based functions like quality, clinical, R&D), companies can simplify operations, accelerate growth, and effectively integrate M&A. This model is uniquely positioned to capture AI value, as it provides the necessary process and data foundations for scalable AI deployment, making it a strategic imperative for competitive advantage in the sector.
viewpoints.source_title: Enterprise Shared Services in Medtech: The Only Wrong Move Is Standing Still

viewpoints.title: Healthcare RCM needs strategic outsourcing and AI to manage pressure
viewpoints.description: McKinsey states that healthcare revenue cycle management (RCM) is undergoing a structural shift, moving from a back-office function to a core strategic enabler. This transition is driven by sustained margin pressure, evolving regulatory requirements, and dynamic reimbursement complexities. Care delivery organizations are responding by pairing measured AI investment with integrated outsourcing strategies. While AI adoption is a priority, expectations for immediate ROI are tempering, highlighting the need for a holistic approach that balances technology, operational execution, and scalable platforms.
viewpoints.source_title: Healthcare revenue cycle management at a strategic turning point: Survey insights

viewpoints.title: UK Business & Professional Services poised for growth despite headwinds
viewpoints.description: Barclays' Head of Business and Professional Services, Stephen Ainsworth, expresses a cautious yet optimistic outlook for the sector in 2026. Despite ongoing headwinds, he believes there are unprecedented opportunities for businesses that prioritize understanding their organizations, embracing technology, and maintaining strong client and team relationships. The sector is seeing increased private equity interest and consolidation, driven by predictable revenues and efficiency gains through technology. This strategic focus is expected to position firms well for future growth and competitiveness.

viewpoints.title: UK financial and professional services growth stalled, action needed
viewpoints.description: TheCityUK and PwC assert that the UK's financial and related professional services industry, a strategic national asset, has seen its growth stall over the last decade, falling behind global competitors. This erosion is due to geopolitical volatility, protectionism, regulatory fragmentation, and technological disruption (AI, DLT). Urgent and decisive action on policy and regulatory reform, coupled with greater ambition and pace, particularly in digital wholesale markets and tokenised assets, could unlock up to £53 billion in additional economic output by 2035, reversing the current trajectory.
viewpoints.source_title: No time to lose: Reasserting UK leadership in financial and related professional services

demand_drivers.driver: Margin pressure and acquisition debt for clients
demand_drivers.description: Companies, particularly in Medtech, are facing significant margin contraction and complexity from acquisition-led growth, driving the need for operational simplification and cost reduction through shared services.
The executive mandate to scale AI requires strong process and data foundations, which enterprise shared services can provide, making them critical platforms for AI deployment and value capture.

new_opportunities.description: Opportunities exist to extend shared services beyond traditional G&A functions to high-value areas like quality management, clinical and regulatory activities (e.g., clinical trial design, regulatory submissions), and R&D functions (e.g., prototype development, product analytics), especially with increasing AI capabilities for knowledge workers.

market_sizing.methodology: Mature shared services organizations have consistently reduced costs by 20% to 40%. This highlights the potential value and cost savings that BPO and shared services can deliver to client organizations, indicating a strong value proposition rather than a market size figure. These savings can then be reinvested or contribute to margin expansion for clients.
market_sizing.source_title: Enterprise Shared Services in Medtech: The Only Wrong Move Is Standing Still

demand_drivers.description: The complex regulatory environment in financial services drives demand for specialized accounting and legal services, including process-driven support which can be outsourced.
Ongoing business activity, M&A, and infrastructure investment create demand for legal, accounting, and advisory services to support transactions, compliance, and strategic planning.

Increasing use of AI in legal services (e.g., document review, contract analysis, research) and other professional services drives demand for technology-enabled solutions, often delivered by specialized providers, including LPO.

new_opportunities.description: The rising adoption of ALSPs by law firms and corporate legal departments for specialized knowledge, cost-effectiveness, and capacity to handle large volumes of work (e.g., document review, contract analysis, legal research) represents a direct opportunity for Legal Process Outsourcing (LPO).

market_sizing.methodology: UK real output contribution (GVA) for professional services directly related to financial services, which include segments relevant to BPO. These figures represent the overall market for these professional services, not exclusively the outsourced components. Accounting services contributed £31.7 billion, management consulting £20.2 billion, and legal services £38.1 billion in 2025.
market_sizing.source_title: Key facts about UK-based financial and related professional services 2026

demand_drivers.description: Small and medium businesses (SMBs) increasingly prefer embedded financial services and value-added services within their software platforms for ease of use and better support, consolidating various operational needs.

Software platforms are embedding financial services and VAS directly into merchant workflows, gaining control over customer relationships and driving rapid revenue growth, impacting how BPO-like services are delivered.

new_opportunities.description: BPO providers specializing in financial processes can develop and offer a modular catalog of value-added services (e.g., payroll, fraud prevention, analytics) built on a shared data foundation, enabling real-time personalization and insights for clients, either directly or by partnering with platforms.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Offering a modular, API-enabled VAS catalog

new_opportunities.description: Opportunity to integrate banking capabilities with specialized software to offer full-service merchant propositions in specific verticals, unlocking new growth and defending existing revenues by meeting comprehensive client needs.

market_sizing.methodology: Projected revenue mix for merchant acquiring in the US. Value-added services (VAS) are projected to reach 30-35% of revenue by 2027, and embedded financial services (e.g., business accounts, commercial cards, lending, payroll, invoicing) are projected to reach 10-20% by 2027. Europe is following a similar trajectory. These categories include services like payroll, fraud prevention, and dispute management that are often part of BPO offerings.
market_sizing.source_title: Global Payments Report 2025: The Future Is (Anything but) Stable
